Fuel cells · Commercial

Molten carbonate fuel cell · MCFC

Carbonate ions move to the fuel electrode as fuel's chemical energy becomes electricity.

Animated operating principles

Ion and electron pathways

CO₃²⁻ · electrolyte / membrane Electrons e⁻ · external circuit

Simplified reaction directions and pathways. Actual particle numbers and speeds differ.

Electrode and electrolyte principles

CO₃²⁻ moves from the air electrode to the fuel electrode in hot molten carbonate.

Air electrode: ½O₂ + CO₂ + 2e⁻ → CO₃²⁻ / Fuel electrode: H₂ + CO₃²⁻ → H₂O + CO₂ + 2e⁻

Advantages

Large distributed generation and high-temperature waste-heat recovery

Drawbacks & challenges

Life and maintenance challenges from corrosive electrolyte and high temperatures

Materials & supply constraints

Uses materials such as nickel; designs need not require precious-metal catalysts

Main applications

Industrial and building distributed generation
